name: Steam runtime (fetched from Valve by the console)
notes: The Valve files the Steam engine needs. Our repository publishes only their hashes; the console fetches the bytes from Valve's own client-update CDN. Pinned to SteamCMD's steamcmd_bins_win32 package of 2026-01-30 (steamclient 10.41.26.25): the build every RVA in gh_steam_engine.h / GREENHOUSE.md 25.5 and 26.10 was reverse-engineered on. A different build is refused, not installed. #277 (1.0.1.0): no patch any more -- the file stays byte-identical to Valve's, signature intact, because a SteamStub-wrapped game verifies the file behind steamclient64's CreateInterface. The slim Xbox user32 has no MapVirtualKeyExA, so the OS loader refuses the pristine DLL and the loader self-maps it instead, bedding that one import in memory (GhSelfMapDll). 1.0.0.0, with the import renamed on disk, stays published for rollback. #278 (1.0.2.0): steam.exe joins the add-on, Valve's own bootstrapper from the steam_client_win32 manifest's steam_win32/steamrow package (IsBootstrapperPackage, client version 1769731672). It is NEVER run -- the Steam client on the console is our own in-process engine -- it is there because a SteamStub-wrapped game checks that a steam.exe exists at the install path it reads from HKLM\Software\Valve\Steam (Dead as Disco: GetFileAttributesW MISSING -> exit 53, s973). Per-file 'source' is how one add-on pins two vendor zips.
